title: Nodeless d-wave pairing in monolayer FeSe revealed by intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry
authors: Runxin Li, Yuchen Huo, Jiong Mei, Ming-Qiang Ren, Miaomiao Wang, Quanxing Wei, Fengyu Yao, Maowen Zheng, Qing Qu, Cui Ding, Hongtao Yuan, Zhuoyu Chen, Wei-Qiang Chen, Kun Jiang, Qi-Kun Xue, Yu-Jie Sun
abstract: The Josephson effect provides a direct phase-sensitive probe of superconducting order and has played a central role in identifying unconventional pairing symmetries1-6. Conventional Josephson interferometry, however, extracts phase information through engineered junction geometries and crystallographic orientations, rather than by resolving the internal phase structure of the pair state within a single unit cell. Here, we use a superconducting Nb tip to realize atomic-scale Josephson interferometry in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3. Despite a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum, the local Josephson response exhibits a striking intra-unit-cell pattern, with maxima centred on Fe-Fe bonds and robust nodal lines along the Fe-Se directions. We show that these nodal lines arise from destructive interference between Josephson tunnelling amplitudes associated with opposite-sign pairing components. Microscopic calculations reproduce the observed spatial pattern and identify it as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing. Our results establish intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry as a local phase-sensitive probe of pairing symmetry in unconventional superconductors.
summary: The authors developed and applied intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry to map the superconducting order parameter in monolayer FeSe. They found a characteristic nodal pattern in the local Josephson response, which theory confirms is the signature of nodeless d-wave pairing. This work establishes a powerful new tool for probing the microscopic phase structure of unconventional superconductors.
main_problem: To develop a local, phase-sensitive probe capable of distinguishing unconventional superconducting pairing symmetries within a single unit cell.
main_result: The local Josephson response exhibits a characteristic intra-unit-cell nodal pattern, which is identified as a fingerprint of nodeless d-wave pairing in monolayer FeSe.
method: Intra-unit-cell Josephson interferometry using a superconducting tip (Nb) on the FeSe/SrTiO3 interface, combined with theoretical modeling.
model_or_system: The system is monolayer FeSe on SrTiO3, modeled using a minimal single-orbital approach with a d-wave pair potential ($\Delta(\mathbf{k}) \propto \cos k_x - \cos k_y$).
key_observables: Local Josephson conductance ($g_0(\mathbf{r})$) and Andreev conductance ($g_A(\mathbf{r})$) mapped across the unit cell.
important_parameters: Temperature ($\sim 30 	ext{ mK}$), junction resistance ($R_N$), and the relative phase between microscopic pairing components.
main_assumptions: The observed pattern is attributed to destructive interference between Josephson tunneling amplitudes associated with opposite-sign pairing components, and the model neglects spin-orbit coupling.
figures_summary: Figures show spatial maps of the Josephson response exhibiting nodal lines along Fe–Se directions and maxima at Fe–Fe bonds, matching theoretical calculations for d-wave pairing.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the technique by showing the Josephson response, then uses theoretical calculations based on d-wave pairing to reproduce the observed nodal pattern, contrasting it with s-wave references.
why_interesting: The technique provides a novel, real-space probe for superconducting phase structure, which is crucial for understanding unconventional pairing mechanisms beyond simple gap measurements.
